subject: Mutual Action Plan & Commit Pathway — Crescent Health
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: julia.mallory@crescenthealth.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan & initial timeline

Hi Julia —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, I put together a concise mutual action plan (MAP) that ties your evaluation milestones to incremental commit thresholds and the discount schedule we discussed. The goal is to make staging → pilot → production ramp predictable for both teams and to surface the renewal/expansion uplift triggers early.

High-level ask: can Crescent confirm target pilot start week of May 24 and a production rollout window in June (conditional on pilot metrics)? If so we'll lock in the commit thresholds outlined in the attached MAP and draft SOW.

What I attached: MAP-draft-v3.xlsx (milestones + pricing tiers), SOW draft (scope & timeline).

Next steps I propose:
- Crescent: confirm pilot start date and success metrics (availability, average latency p95, and request throughput).
- Redwood: finalize GPU profile and onboarding runbook; provide SOC2 evidence stub for procurement.
- Both: align on a signing window by May 20 to enable reserved capacity planning.

I'll loop in Aditya (SE) and Marcus (AEs) for technical and commercial details.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): MAP-draft-v3.xlsx, SOW-Crescent-Health-draft.pdf
From: julia.mallory@crescenthealth.com
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@crescenthealth.com, oliver@consults.ai
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & initial timeline

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the MAP — this format helps. A few clarifying requests from my side and from procurement:

1) Discount schedule: procurement wants to see an explicit table that ties committed monthly throughput (tokens or requests) to discount tiers and the timing of when discounts apply. Can you move the threshold to be aligned on monthly committed units rather than cumulative across pilot + prod?

2) Ramp definition: we need a precise definition of "pilot success" (sample size, duration, SLA targets). Can the MAP include the measurement window (14 days after pilot start) and the minimum traffic required?

3) SOC2 / security evidence: procurement asked for the SOC2 summary report and a point of contact for a short questionnaire.

We are aligned on a May production window in principle, but procurement requires the SOW and more explicit commit language before we can sign by the 20th. Oliver is helping on the commercial terms and wanted to confirm: if Crescent commits to a 6-month minimum at X throughput, what is the maximum uplift discount applicable at renewal?

I can take a stab at internal alignment this week if you can send an updated MAP that addresses the three points above.

—Julia
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: julia.mallory@crescenthealth.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & initial timeline

Hi Julia — thanks, great questions. Attached is MAP-draft-v3.xlsx (updated) and a sample SOW. Summary of changes inline below.

Quoted for context: "1) Discount schedule... move threshold to monthly committed units" — Done. The MAP now includes a monthly committed-unit table and the specific billing measurement (tokens per 30-day calendar window). Discount tiers are applied to recurring monthly invoices and require meeting the committed throughput for that month to earn the tier.

Key commerce points (high level):
- Pilot (2-week window, 14-day measurement after pilot launch): success metrics = p95 latency <= 220ms, service availability >= 99.5%, and request sample >= 100k tokens/day averaged over measurement window.
- Pilot to Prod conversion: upon meeting pilot criteria, Crescent can sign a 3-month initial commit (monthly throughput X) which qualifies for Tier 1 discount (7%).
- Ramp & Renewal uplift: if Crescent increases committed monthly throughput by >= 50% at renewal (month‑to‑month or at term renewal) and sustains it for 2 consecutive months, Redwood will apply a one-time renewal uplift discount of an additional 3% for the next term (subject to SKU parity).
- Maximum uplift at renewal (combined with base discount): up to 10% total (7% base + up to 3% uplift) for customers who meet commit/rate thresholds.

Operational notes:
- Reserved capacity onboarding requires DocuSign by May 20 to guarantee the GPU pool for June rollout. If signing slips past May 27, reserved capacity can be accommodated but lead times increase (possible 2-week delay).
- SOC2: attached is a SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf and a single point of contact (security@redwoodinference.com) for the short questionnaire.

Attached: MAP-draft-v3.xlsx (updated), SOW-Crescent-Health-draft.pdf, SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf

If that addresses the procurement asks, can Crescent confirm a signing target of May 20 and pilot start week of May 24? Once we have that I'll open the DocuSign envelope and set the onboarding kickoff.

Thanks —
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): MAP-draft-v3.xlsx, SOW-Crescent-Health-draft.pdf, SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf
From: procurement@crescenthealth.com
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, julia.mallory@crescenthealth.com
Cc: oliver@consults.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & initial timeline

Laura / Julia —

Thanks for the quick update. Procurement has two additional requests before we move to sign:

- Please convert the monthly-commit language into a short contract addendum (one page) that we can include with the SOW; it should specify measurement window, meter, and remedy if minimum committed units are not met in a month (credit vs. true-up).
- We also request a 30-day pilot cancellation clause with no penalty (we may exercise this if pilot criteria are not met).

On uplift: the 3% one-time renewal uplift is acceptable in principle, but we need language that ties the uplift to verifiable telemetry (Redwood API usage logs) and a definition of "sustain for 2 consecutive months" (calendar months vs rolling 60-day window).

Please provide the contract addendum and the contract language clarifying telemetry and the measurement window. If you can send by COB May 12 we'll route internally for signoff.

Procurement (Crescent Health)
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: procurement@crescenthealth.com, julia.mallory@crescenthealth.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & initial timeline

Hi team —

Appreciate the clarity. We've prepared the one-page addendum and a short contract clause describing the telemetry measurement (calendar month windows, API usage logs with daily rollups, and a 30-day credit remedy for under-delivery). Attached to this thread: SOW-Crescent-Health-draft.pdf (updated) and MAP-draft-v3.xlsx (final v3).

A few commitments from Redwood:
- We will implement the telemetry export to provide daily usage CSVs during onboarding period and continue as part of the admin console.
- We accept a 30-day pilot cancellation right (no penalty) and will include it in the SOW addendum.
- We will use calendar-month windows for uplift verification; "sustain for 2 consecutive months" means two full calendar months meeting the committed monthly throughput.

Next steps:
1) I'll share a DocuSign envelope with the updated SOW + addendum by EOD May 12.
2) Crescent to sign by May 20 to guarantee reserved capacity for the June rollout.
3) Onboarding kickoff meeting (30m) scheduled for May 24 once signature is complete.

If that works I'll issue the DocuSign link to Julia and Procurement and cc the SE for the kickoff invite.

Best —
Laura

Attachment(s): SOW-Crescent-Health-draft.pdf (updated), MAP-draft-v3.xlsx (final v3)
